posts.message: Clubs spend over $100 million a year answering routine member phone calls.
posts.angle: A light stat card with the NGF figure as the number and routine member phone calls as the label. The caption names the small questions behind the figure without blaming staff or members.

posts.message: Every club has members who read every word the club sends and members who never open any of it.
posts.angle: A recognition carousel: the photo cover introduces the familiar members, one type per slide, and the close lands on each one deserving an answer where they are.
posts.photoBrief: Golfers together on a sunny course, a familiar club scene.
posts.artDirectionMatch: Club members on the course, the people the carousel describes.

posts.message: A question the assistant hands off arrives in the club inbox inside the same conversation, so staff reply without starting over.
posts.angle: The escalation thread from the staff side: the member asks something the club has not published, the assistant hands it to the team, and the caption explains that staff pick it up in the same conversation.
posts.operationalCheck: ops-question-timing: the member asks about an event the club has not announced yet, so the only honest reply is a handoff to staff.

posts.message: A member mid-round can get the grill hours by text before the round is over.
posts.angle: Two golfers talking on the course, with a thread: a member asks if the grill serves lunch after they finish and the club answers from the dining hours.
posts.photoBrief: Two golfers together on the course in daylight.
posts.artDirectionMatch: Two golfers talking mid-round on the course, the moment a lunch question comes up.
posts.operationalCheck: ops-round-ends-18th: the round ends on the 18th hole, so a lunch question asked on the ninth is about after the round.

posts.message: We are building toward email, text, the app and AI Assist sharing one inbox and one member history.
posts.angle: The communication hub: four channel tiles joining one inbox panel, framed as the direction Club Pilot is building in, not a shipped feature.

posts.pillar: Operator POV, day in the life
posts.message: A club answers the same handful of member questions every week, and each one lands on a busy person.
posts.angle: A list carousel: one routine question per slide, then a close about the interruption and a technique to count them.

posts.message: The questions members ask change with the season, so the answers a club keeps current have to change too.
posts.angle: A reveal-flip carousel over a late-season course: what members ask in the fall, the answer (whatever changed last), and the seasonal review as the takeaway.
posts.photoBrief: A course in low golden light with long shadows.
posts.artDirectionMatch: A course in low late-season light, matching the question about the fall.

posts.message: Golf Digest included Club Pilot in its 2026 PGA Merchandise Show roundup.
posts.angle: The proof bar with the locked Golf Digest quote and attribution over the Golf Digest and Golf Bizz Review logos. The caption carries the single demo link of the batch.

posts.message: Every club has a group devoted enough to play through conditions everyone else waits out.
posts.angle: A foggy tennis court, full bleed, with one flat line about the regulars who play anyway.
posts.photoBrief: A tennis court in thick fog with players on it.
posts.artDirectionMatch: A fog-covered court with players on it, the scene the line describes.

posts.pillar: Operator POV, day in the life
posts.message: A Sunday evening question about Monday morning can be answered from the club's hours without interrupting anyone's evening.
posts.angle: A dark message thread: a member asks on Sunday night when the fitness center opens and the club answers from the facility hours.
posts.operationalCheck: ops-question-timing: the member asks on Sunday evening because that is when Monday morning becomes relevant.
